title: Exact count matching left the response link to adult count disagreement unresolved in 538 worm pairs
abstract: We tested the link between adult chemical count disagreement and evoked response detection within exact summed-count strata. We linked two adult Witvliet maps to the Randi wild-type response atlas by cell name. Of 760 both-present pairs, 538 had within-count disagreement variation. These pairs had 40 detections and 36 count strata. The detection-probability slope per 0.1 disagreement was +0.000626. A conditional 95 percent cell-family bootstrap interval was -0.021956 to +0.026232. Four specified checks also left the sign unresolved. The test addresses the count-overlap limit of an earlier regression on the same data. It does not provide independent biological replication. Different animals supplied anatomy and activity. Sparse responses, omitted covariates, two anatomy samples and fixed atlas estimates limit inference. New code, aggregate results, a figure and exact source hashes support reproduction. External records remain outside the baseline bundle.

display.caption: Exact-count slopes and conditional cell-family bootstrap intervals. All five intervals cross zero. Positive slopes indicate more detections with greater count disagreement. These intervals do not estimate variation across animals.

citations.reason: Tests its reported count-overlap limitation using an exact-stratum statistic and a recomputed bootstrap. No code or numeric tables reused.
Context for pooled functional data and cross-animal linkage.
